WEBSITE/APP PRIVACY POLICY — CCPA CONSUMER-FACING DISCLOSURE
Prepared for Acme, Inc. · Identifiers (name, email address), internet activity (browsing history on our site), and geolocation data

PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF THIS PRIVACY NOTICE
This Website/App Privacy Policy and Notice at Collection ("Notice") describes how Acme, Inc. collects, uses, and discloses personal information about consumers who visit or use Acme, Inc.'s website or application, and describes the rights California consumers have with respect to that personal information under the California Consumer Privacy Act, as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act (California Civil Code § 1798.100 et seq.). Consumers with questions about this Notice, or who wish to exercise a right described in it, may contact Acme, Inc. as follows: privacy@acme.com or (415) 555-0100. This Notice is directed to consumers and does not itself set out the contract terms between Acme, Inc. and any vendor or service provider that processes personal information on Acme, Inc.'s behalf; those terms are addressed in a separate document.

THE NOTICE-AT-COLLECTION REQUIREMENT
California law requires that a business that controls the collection of a consumer's personal information inform consumers, at or before the point of collection, of the categories of personal information to be collected and the purposes for which those categories of personal information are collected or used, and whether that information is sold or shared. If the business collects sensitive personal information, the same at-or-before-collection notice must separately identify the categories of sensitive personal information to be collected and the purposes for which they are collected or used, and whether that information is sold or shared. The same notice must also state the length of time the business intends to retain each category of personal information, or, if that is not possible, the criteria used to determine that retention period. A business may not collect additional categories of personal information, or use personal information for additional purposes, that are incompatible with the disclosed purpose, without providing a further notice consistent with this requirement. Separately, the statute allows a business that, acting as a third party, controls the collection of personal information about a consumer to satisfy this notice obligation by providing the required information prominently and conspicuously on the homepage of its internet website, and imposes an at-the-location notice duty on a third party that collects personal information on its own premises.

A business shall not collect additional categories of personal information or use personal information collected for additional purposes that are incompatible with the disclosed purpose for which the personal information was collected without providing the consumer with notice consistent with this section. (2) If the business collects sensitive personal information, the categories of sensitive personal information to be collected and the purposes for which the categories of sensitive personal information are collected or used, and whether that information is sold or shared. A business shall not collect additional categories of sensitive personal information or use sensitive personal information collected for additional purposes that are incompatible with the disclosed purpose for which the sensitive personal information was collected without providing the consumer with notice consistent with this section. (3) The length of time the business intends to retain each category of personal information, including sensitive personal information, or if that is not possible, the criteria used to determine that period provided that a business shall not retain a consumer’s personal information or sensitive personal information for each disclosed purpose for which the personal information was collected for longer than is reasonably necessary for that disclosed purpose."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.100(a) (official leginfo.legislature.ca.gov text), California Consumer Privacy Act, point-of-collection notice content requirement (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1798.100.)
  "(b) A business that, acting as a third party, controls the collection of personal information about a consumer may satisfy its obligation under subdivision (a) by providing the required information prominently and conspicuously on the homepage of its internet website. In addition, if a business acting as a third party controls the collection of personal information about a consumer on its premises, including in a vehicle, then the business shall, at or before the point of collection, inform consumers as to the categories of personal information to be collected and the purposes for which the categories of personal information are used, and whether that personal information is sold, in a clear and conspicuous manner at the location."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.100(b) (official leginfo.legislature.ca.gov text), California Consumer Privacy Act, homepage-posting alternative for a third party controlling collection (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1798.100.)

This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of California's CCPA/CPRA consumer-facing disclosure requirements — not a claim about which state's law governs a specific business; other states now have their own, differently-structured privacy statutes, and this document addresses California's CCPA/CPRA only. This clause does not determine whether a specific business meets the CCPA's revenue or volume thresholds to qualify as a "business" subject to this title in the first place, whether a specific business is acting as a first party or a third party with respect to a specific collection, or whether the homepage-posting alternative in subdivision (b) is available for a specific collection — those are fact-specific determinations this document does not make. CATEGORIES OF PERSONAL INFORMATION COLLECTED AND PURPOSES OF USE
At or before the point Acme, Inc. collects personal information from a consumer through its website or application, Acme, Inc. discloses the following categories of personal information collected: Identifiers (name, email address), internet activity (browsing history on our site), and geolocation data. Acme, Inc. collects and uses those categories of personal information for the following purposes: Providing and improving our services, processing transactions, and customer support. Acme, Inc. does not collect additional categories of personal information, or use personal information collected for additional purposes, that are incompatible with the purposes disclosed above without providing consumers a further notice. Whether any category of personal information identified above is sold or shared with third parties, and the length of time Acme, Inc. intends to retain each category, are addressed elsewhere in this Notice.

CONSUMER RIGHTS TO DELETE, CORRECT, AND KNOW WHAT PERSONAL INFORMATION IS COLLECTED, SOLD, OR SHARED
California law gives consumers four related rights concerning personal information a business has collected about them. First, a consumer has the right to request that a business delete personal information the business has collected from the consumer. Second, a consumer has the right to request that a business that maintains inaccurate personal information about the consumer correct that inaccurate personal information, taking into account the nature of the personal information and the purposes of processing it. Third, a consumer has the right to request that a business that collects personal information about the consumer disclose the categories of personal information it has collected about that consumer, the categories of sources from which that information is collected, the business or commercial purpose for collecting, selling, or sharing it, the categories of third parties to whom the business discloses it, and the specific pieces of personal information the business has collected about that consumer. Fourth, a consumer has the right to request that a business that sells or shares the consumer's personal information, or discloses it for a business purpose, disclose the categories of personal information sold, shared, or disclosed for a business purpose, and the categories of third parties or persons to whom it was sold, shared, or disclosed.

This clause does not restate the statutory exceptions to the deletion right (Civil Code § 1798.105(d)), which permit a business to decline a deletion request for reasons such as completing a transaction, security, debugging, free speech, legal compliance, and certain research uses — those exceptions exist in the statute's text but were not independently quoted or verified for this clause, and this document does not represent that they do or do not apply to any specific deletion request. No case law was checked on any of these four provisions; each statute's own text is unambiguous, so the statutes stand as the source here without a corroborating case.

STATEMENT OF CONSUMER RIGHTS AND HOW TO EXERCISE THEM
Consumers whose personal information Acme, Inc. collects have the right to: request deletion of personal information Acme, Inc. has collected from the consumer; request correction of inaccurate personal information Acme, Inc. maintains about the consumer; request disclosure of the categories and specific pieces of personal information Acme, Inc. has collected about the consumer; request disclosure of the categories of personal information Acme, Inc. has sold, shared, or disclosed for a business purpose, and the categories of third parties or persons to whom it was sold, shared, or disclosed; direct Acme, Inc. not to sell or share the consumer's personal information; and direct Acme, Inc. to limit its use of the consumer's sensitive personal information, to the extent Acme, Inc. uses sensitive personal information for purposes beyond those necessary to provide the goods or services requested. A consumer, or a person authorized by the consumer to act on the consumer's behalf, may submit a request to exercise any of these rights as follows: privacy@acme.com or (415) 555-0100.

CONSUMER RIGHTS TO OPT OUT OF SALE OR SHARING AND TO LIMIT USE OF SENSITIVE PERSONAL INFORMATION
California law gives a consumer the right, at any time, to direct a business that sells or shares the consumer's personal information to third parties not to sell or share it — a right the statute calls the right to opt out of sale or sharing. Separately, California law gives a consumer the right, at any time, to direct a business that collects sensitive personal information about the consumer to limit its use of that sensitive personal information to the use necessary to perform the goods or services reasonably expected by an average consumer requesting them, along with certain other statutorily authorized uses; a business that uses or discloses a consumer's sensitive personal information for purposes beyond those specified must provide notice of that use and of the consumer's right to limit it.

THE "DO NOT SELL OR SHARE MY PERSONAL INFORMATION" LINK, AND THE OPT-OUT PREFERENCE SIGNAL ALTERNATIVE
A business that sells or shares consumers' personal information, or that uses or discloses sensitive personal information for purposes beyond those the statute authorizes without a consumer's separate direction, must provide a clear and conspicuous link on the business's internet homepages, titled "Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information," to a web page that lets a consumer opt out of the sale or sharing of the consumer's personal information; a second, separately titled link, "Limit the Use of My Sensitive Personal Information"; or, at the business's discretion, a single combined link in place of the first two. As an alternative to posting these links, the statute provides that a business is not required to comply with the link-posting requirement if the business instead allows consumers to opt out of the sale or sharing of their personal information, and to limit the use of their sensitive personal information, through an "opt-out preference signal" — a signal sent, with the consumer's consent, by a platform, technology, or mechanism meeting technical specifications set out in regulations, indicating the consumer's intent to opt out or to limit use.

REQUIRED CONTENT OF A BUSINESS'S ONLINE PRIVACY POLICY
California law requires a business to disclose specific information in its online privacy policy or policies, or, if it has none, on its internet website, and to update that information at least once every 12 months. The required content includes: a description of the consumer's rights to know, delete, correct, access, and opt out described elsewhere in this Notice, together with two or more designated methods for submitting requests to exercise them (subject to a narrower, email-only alternative for a business that operates exclusively online and has a direct relationship with the consumer); a list of the categories of personal information the business has collected about consumers in the preceding 12 months, the categories of sources of that information, the business or commercial purpose for collecting, selling, or sharing it, and the categories of third parties to whom the business discloses it; a separate list of the categories of personal information the business has sold or shared about consumers in the preceding 12 months (or, if none, a statement to that effect); and a separate list of the categories of personal information the business has disclosed about consumers for a business purpose in the preceding 12 months (or, if none, a statement to that effect).

NON-DISCRIMINATION FOR EXERCISING CCPA RIGHTS, AND THE FINANCIAL INCENTIVE EXCEPTION
California law prohibits a business from discriminating against a consumer because the consumer exercised any right the CCPA/CPRA gives consumers, including by denying goods or services to the consumer, charging the consumer different prices or rates for goods or services (including through discounts, other benefits, or penalties), providing a different level or quality of goods or services to the consumer, or suggesting that the consumer will receive any of those different treatments. Separately, and as a limited exception to that general prohibition, the statute permits a business to offer financial incentives — including payments to consumers as compensation — for the collection, sale, sharing, or retention of personal information, and permits a business to offer a different price, rate, level, or quality of goods or services if that difference is reasonably related to the value the consumer's data provides to the business. A business offering such a financial incentive program must notify consumers of the incentive, may enter a consumer into the program only with the consumer's prior opt-in consent that clearly describes the program's material terms, and must allow the consumer to revoke that consent at any time; if a consumer refuses to provide opt-in consent, the business must wait at least 12 months before asking the consumer to provide it again.

Acme, Inc. does not collect additional categories of personal information, or use personal information collected for additional purposes, that are incompatible with the purposes disclosed above without providing consumers a further notice. Whether any category of personal information identified above is sold or shared with third parties, and the length of time Acme, Inc. intends to retain each category, are addressed elsewhere in this Notice.

California law gives consumers four related rights concerning personal information a business has collected about them. First, a consumer has the right to request that a business delete personal information the business has collected from the consumer. Second, a consumer has the right to request that a business that maintains inaccurate personal information about the consumer correct that inaccurate personal information, taking into account the nature of the personal information and the purposes of processing it. Third, a consumer has the right to request that a business that collects personal information about the consumer disclose the categories of personal information it has collected about that consumer, the categories of sources from which that information is collected, the business or commercial purpose for collecting, selling, or sharing it, the categories of third parties to whom the business discloses it, and the specific pieces of personal information the business has collected about that consumer. Fourth, a consumer has the right to request that a business that sells or shares the consumer's personal information, or discloses it for a business purpose, disclose the categories of personal information sold, shared, or disclosed for a business purpose, and the categories of third parties or persons to whom it was sold, shared, or disclosed.

Separately, California law gives a consumer the right, at any time, to direct a business that collects sensitive personal information about the consumer to limit its use of that sensitive personal information to the use necessary to perform the goods or services reasonably expected by an average consumer requesting them, along with certain other statutorily authorized uses; a business that uses or discloses a consumer's sensitive personal information for purposes beyond those specified must provide notice of that use and of the consumer's right to limit it.

expectedJSON.body: California law prohibits a business from discriminating against a consumer because the consumer exercised any right the CCPA/CPRA gives consumers, including by denying goods or services to the consumer, charging the consumer different prices or rates for goods or services (including through discounts, other benefits, or penalties), providing a different level or quality of goods or services to the consumer, or suggesting that the consumer will receive any of those different treatments. Separately, and as a limited exception to that general prohibition, the statute permits a business to offer financial incentives — including payments to consumers as compensation — for the collection, sale, sharing, or retention of personal information, and permits a business to offer a different price, rate, level, or quality of goods or services if that difference is reasonably related to the value the consumer's data provides to the business. A business offering such a financial incentive program must notify consumers of the incentive, may enter a consumer into the program only with the consumer's prior opt-in consent that clearly describes the program's material terms, and must allow the consumer to revoke that consent at any time; if a consumer refuses to provide opt-in consent, the business must wait at least 12 months before asking the consumer to provide it again.

citations.quote: (a) (1) A business shall not discriminate against a consumer because the consumer exercised any of the consumer’s rights under this title, including, but not limited to, by: (A) Denying goods or services to the consumer. (B) Charging different prices or rates for goods or services, including through the use of discounts or other benefits or imposing penalties. (C) Providing a different level or quality of goods or services to the consumer. (D) Suggesting that the consumer will receive a different price or rate for goods or services or a different level or quality of goods or services. (E) Retaliating against an employee, applicant for employment, or independent contractor, as defined in subparagraph (A) of paragraph (2) of subdivision (m) of Section 1798.145, for exercising their rights under this title.

A business may also offer a different price, rate, level, or quality of goods or services to the consumer if that price or difference is reasonably related to the value provided to the business by the consumer’s data. (2) A business that offers any financial incentives pursuant to this subdivision, shall notify consumers of the financial incentives pursuant to Section 1798.130. (3) A business may enter a consumer into a financial incentive program only if the consumer gives the business prior opt-in consent pursuant to Section 1798.130 that clearly describes the material terms of the financial incentive program, and which may be revoked by the consumer at any time.
